installation.note: rmdir is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: rmdir (remove directory) deletes empty directories only. Unlike rm -r, rmdir is safer because it only removes directories that are completely empty. This prevents accidental deletion of directories with contents. For non-empty directories, use rm -r instead.
when_to_use: Remove directories without risk of deleting files
Ensure directory is truly empty before removal
Safer alternative to rm -r for empty directories

misconceptions.title: rmdir removes directories with contents
misconceptions.misconception: rmdir can delete directories that have files in them
misconceptions.reality: rmdir only removes empty directories. For directories with contents, use rm -r instead. This is a safety feature.
misconceptions.tip: rmdir = remove empty directories only. rm -r = remove directories with contents.

misconceptions.title: rmdir needs -r flag like rm
misconceptions.reality: rmdir works on directories by default (but only empty ones). It doesn't need -r. The -r flag is for rm, not rmdir.
misconceptions.tip: rmdir works on directories directly - no special flags needed, but directory must be empty

misconceptions.title: rmdir is the same as rm -r
misconceptions.misconception: rmdir and rm -r do the same thing
misconceptions.reality: rmdir only removes empty directories (safer). rm -r removes directories with all contents (powerful but dangerous).
misconceptions.tip: Use rmdir for empty directories (safer). Use rm -r for directories with contents (dangerous).

common_pitfalls.description: rmdir fails when directory has files or subdirectories
common_pitfalls.solution: Check if directory is empty with ls first. Use rm -r to remove directories with contents, or delete contents first then use rmdir.
Use rmdir -p to remove directory and all empty parents in the path. This cleans up the entire structure.

common_pitfalls.description: Directory appears empty but has hidden files (.files)
common_pitfalls.solution: Use ls -a to see hidden files. Remove them first, or use rm -r if you want to remove everything including hidden files.

common_pitfalls.description: Cannot remove directory due to permissions
common_pitfalls.solution: Use sudo if you need to remove system directories, or check permissions with ls -ld. You need write permission on parent directory.

additional_notes.safety_feature: rmdir only removes empty directories - this is a safety feature to prevent accidental deletion of files
additional_notes.empty_requirement: Directory must be completely empty (no files, no subdirectories, including hidden files)
additional_notes.hidden_files: Hidden files (starting with .) will prevent rmdir from working - check with ls -a
additional_notes.parent_removal: The -p flag removes empty parent directories recursively, working backwards up the path
additional_notes.comparison: rmdir is safer than rm -r because it only works on empty directories. Use rm -r for directories with contents.
additional_notes.alternatives: For non-empty directories, use rm -r (dangerous) or delete contents first then rmdir (safer)
